title: District 7 After Dark
briefing: A neighborhood review follows the city's earlier concentrated residential outage. Residents report spoiled medicine and failed home equipment. Engineers need continued access to the same circuits, while a compensation fund cannot cover every reported loss.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Temporary bypasses can shorten another outage, but installing them uses the crews booked for long-term circuit replacement.
private_intelligence.community: Residents will allow crews through apartment blocks if repair access is separated from compensation eligibility checks.
private_intelligence.economy: A flat compensation payment is quick; case-by-case assessment is cheaper but would take weeks to process.
private_intelligence.safety: Some reported equipment failures require immediate inspection even when the household cannot provide a purchase receipt.

choices.title: Finish the Circuit First
choices.description: Prioritize permanent repairs and compensate only verified critical losses.
choices.consequence: The circuit becomes more dependable, but narrow compensation deepens distrust among residents with undocumented losses.

choices.title: Repair with Community Guarantees
choices.description: Fund bypasses, independent loss review and emergency equipment checks.
choices.consequence: Residents regain a voice and immediate checks reduce harm, while crews and funds move away from permanent renewal.

choices.title: Pay Flat Emergency Grants
choices.description: Issue flat grants while running the existing repair schedule.
choices.consequence: Fast payments ease household hardship and support local trade, but unchanged outage exposure leaves unresolved equipment hazards.
